slot.brief: Solve a homogeneous first-order DE using y = vx substitution and obtain the general solution.

verdicts.working: Set v=y/x. Then x dv/dx=(1+v²)/(1-v), so integrating gives arctan(v)−½ln(1+v²)=ln(x)+C. Since x>0, this is equivalent to option A.

working:
$y=vx$ gives $v+x\dfrac{dv}{dx}=\dfrac{1+v}{1-v}$, so $\dfrac{1-v}{1+v^2}\,dv=\dfrac{dx}{x}$. Thus $\tan^{-1}v-\dfrac12\ln(1+v^2)=\ln x+C$, or $\tan^{-1}(y/x)-\dfrac12\ln(x^2+y^2)=C$.

solution:
Let $y=vx$. Then $v+x\dfrac{dv}{dx}=\dfrac{1+v}{1-v}$, so $\dfrac{1-v}{1+v^2}\,dv=\dfrac{dx}{x}$.
$$\tan^{-1}v-\frac12\ln(1+v^2)=\ln x+C$$
Using $v=\dfrac yx$ and $x>0$, this simplifies to $\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac yx\right)-\dfrac12\ln(x^2+y^2)=C$. (D)
